title_zh: 末班車，從來沒讓我下車
title_en: The Last Bus Never Let Me Off
story_zh: 凌晨十一點四十七分，一輛顯示「末班車」的公車停在我面前。可站牌明明寫著，末班車十點就走了。車門打開，司機的座位空著。我一上車，門就自己關上。車上只有一名濕髮女人，背對著我。下一站到了。女人沒有起身，卻忽然轉頭問我：「你還記得自己在哪裡下車嗎？」她的嘴巴沒有動。我抬頭看後照鏡。鏡子裡，女人正站在我身後；我猛然回頭，座位卻是空的。手機收到一張剛拍的照片。照片裡，我仍坐在車上，而拍照的人，正站在車外的雨裡。我瘋狂按下車鈴。窗玻璃慢慢浮出幾個字：「你還沒下車。」車門始終沒有開。公車駛進沒有路燈的山路，電子站牌突然顯示：「終點站：山林路口。」我終於認出那個站名。三天前的新聞裡，一名女子在山林路口遭末班車撞倒。照片裡的死者，就是我。原來我一直躺在站牌下面，而這輛車，每晚都來接我。
story_en: At 11:47 p.m., a bus marked LAST SERVICE stopped in front of me. But the timetable said the final bus had left almost two hours ago. The doors opened. The driver’s seat was empty. I stepped aboard, and the doors shut on their own. A woman with wet hair sat facing away from me. At the next stop, she turned her head. “Do you remember where you got off?” she asked. Her lips never moved. I glanced at the rearview mirror. She was standing right behind me. I spun around. Her seat was empty. My phone received a photo taken seconds ago. In it, I was still sitting on the bus. Whoever took the picture was standing outside in the rain. I hammered the stop button. Words slowly appeared on the window: YOU HAVEN’T GOTTEN OFF. The doors stayed locked. The bus climbed a road without streetlights. Its display changed: FINAL STOP — FOREST CROSSING. Suddenly, I recognized that name. Three days earlier, a woman had been struck by the last bus at Forest Crossing. The victim in the news photo was me. I was still lying beneath the bus stop sign. And every night, this bus came back for me.
